newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The inflexible positions of Ankara reiterated in Athens yesterday by visiting Deputy Foreign Minister Onur Oymen have placed the rapprochement process back in danger: according to some, this may be exactly what Ankara wants. Oymen refused to withdraw Turkey's threat of war but said he would tell Ankara that Greece had no intention of extending its territorial waters to 12 miles for the time being.
--Some 140,000 pensioners from the public service will receive an average pension increase of 8.0 percent after the readjustment of civil servants' wage scales.

--Oymen's allegations yesterday that Ankara had documents on the status of islets in the Aegean and that Ankara and Athens should sit down to discuss them provoked Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos into calling his comments "a diplomatic pickle".
--Green Party Eurodeputies in Athens yesterday warned of the financial and environmental costs involved with Athens hosting the 2004 Olympic Games.

--The demand for shares of newly-listed Xiosbank on the Athens Stock Exchange soared so high yesterday that it brought down the bourse's electronic transactions systems. Technicians worked through the night to make sure the same thing doesn't happen again today.
--A new study says 3,000 children are involved in prostitution in Greece, the majority of them Greek, a conference on the sexual exploitation of minors in Athens heard.
--Greece reacted with fury yesterday to Oymen's comments which essentially reiterated Turkey's threat of war if Greece extended its territorial waters to 12 nautical miles.

--Dimitra Liani-Papandreou, the widow of late ruling PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou, is busy with her book on her life with her late husband and is not having an affair with a well-known actor, her mother reveals.

--The mother of a 17-year-old boy kept at home 15 days after his death from cancer insisted that he was only in a coma and continued to 'treat' him until the odour of the decomposing body drove neighbours to make the grisly discovery.

--The policeman charged with murdering a colleague in the Greek consulate in Gjirkaster last week broke down and confessed yesterday, saying he shot Nikos Markakis by accident while they were playing around with their guns. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
